title: Perfect generators detect lower cohomological bounds on algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect complex is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Derived tensor and pullback use K-flat resolutions, and derived global sections use K-injective resolutions. Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$. Quasi-compact means every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means the diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $G\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be perfect and a generator, meaning that for every $F$ in this category, vanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}(G[n],F)$ for every integer $n$ implies $F\simeq0$. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the following are equivalent: (i) there is an integer $c$ with $\mathcal H^j(K)=0$ for every $j<c$; (ii) $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(G,K[j])=0$ for every sufficiently negative integer $j$; (iii) $R\Gamma(X,G^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}K)$ is cohomologically bounded below. Here $G^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(G,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and $R\Gamma$ is [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

proof.text: Suppose (i), with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<c$. Apply the finite-window lemma to $P=G$, obtaining $[a,b]$. Since $\mathcal H^q(K[j])=\mathcal H^{q+j}(K)$, this vanishes throughout $[a,b]$ whenever $j<c-b$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}(G,K[j])=0$ for those $j$, proving (ii).

Perfect duality gives the derived isomorphism $G^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\simeq R\mathcal Hom(G,K)$. The global derived-Hom sections model identifies $H^jR\Gamma(X,R\mathcal Hom(G,K))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(G,K[j])$ for every integer $j$. Applying $R\Gamma$ to the displayed isomorphism therefore proves (ii) if and only if (iii), by the definition of bounded-below cohomology. No quasi-coherence of internal Hom or boundedness of $K$ is assumed here.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, second paragraph; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JJ and section-global-RHom.

proof.text: Assume (ii). For any $E\in C_X$ write $T_E(P)$ for eventual vanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}(P,E[j])$ as $j\to-\infty$. This holds for zero, is invariant under isomorphisms, and passes to finite sums and retracts because the corresponding Hom groups are finite sums and retracts. For a shift $P[n]$, use $\operatorname{Hom}(P[n],E[j])=\operatorname{Hom}(P,E[(j)-(n)])$. Exactness of Hom out of distinguished triangles, also after rotating, proves two-out-of-three: choose $j$ smaller than both vanishing bounds, and also their translates by $1$, in the adjacent exact Hom terms. Thus the objects satisfying $T_E$ form a thick subcategory. The classical-generation lemma and (ii) give $T_K(P)$ for every perfect $P$. We shall prove that, on every qcqs algebraic space, this all-perfect-test condition forces a lower bound on $E$.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, third paragraph, (2)--(6) imply (7); written thick-closure argument.

proof.text: First record the truncation consequence needed below. For perfect $P$ and $E\in C_X$, $T_E(P)$ is equivalent to $T_{\tau_{\le a}E}(P)$ for every integer $a$. Indeed the standard truncation triangle is $\tau_{\le a}E\to E\to F\to(\tau_{\le a}E)[1]$, where $F=\tau_{>a}E$ is bounded below. The finite-window argument of step 1, applied to $P$ and $F$, makes $\operatorname{Hom}(P,F[j])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(P,F[j-1])$ vanish for all sufficiently negative $j$. Hom into this triangle and its rotation then identifies the two other Hom groups in these degrees. The truncations have quasi-coherent cohomology because their cohomology sheaves are either those of $E$ or zero.

Apply distinguished-square induction to the isomorphism-invariant property $\mathcal P(W)$: every $E\in C_W$ satisfying $T_E(P)$ for every perfect $P$ is bounded below. The affine base case uses $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $P=\mathcal O_W$. The global-Hom model, with the source structure module in degree zero, computes $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_W,E[j])=H^jR\Gamma(W,E)$. The affine etale derived-module equivalence has quasi-inverse $R\Gamma$; its associated-module functor is exact and faithful. Thus a lower bound for $R\Gamma(W,E)$ gives the same bound for the cohomology sheaves of $E$. This includes the zero ring and the empty affine scheme. It remains to verify the square condition, which steps 6--8 do.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, affine base case, using spaces-perfect.tex Tag 071Q and the affine module equivalence.

proof.text: Let $(i:U\hookrightarrow W,p:V\to W)$ be a square in that induction, and assume $\mathcal P(U)$, $\mathcal P(V)$ and $\mathcal P(U\times_WV)$. Let $E\in C_W$ satisfy all perfect tests. Apply the supported Koszul localization lemma to this square. Its hypotheses are exactly qcqs $W$, quasi-compact open $U$ and affine $V$; its construction gives a perfect $B_W$. The test $T_E(B_W)$ supplies the hypothesis of that lemma and yields an integer $a$ and the canonical isomorphism $\tau_{\le a}E\simeq\tau_{\le a}Ri_*(E|_U)$. This is an isomorphism of derived objects, not merely separate cohomology isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, distinguished-square proof, supported Koszul complex and low-truncation comparison.

proof.text: Put $M=Ri_*(E|_U)$. For every perfect $Q$ on $W$, step 4 and the comparison of step 6 give $T_M(Q)$ from $T_E(Q)$. Here $M\in C_W$ by quasi-coherent direct image: the quasi-compact open immersion into qcqs $W$ is qcqs. For an arbitrary perfect $A$ on $U$, choose $A\xrightarrow{s}i^*Q\xrightarrow{r}A$ with $rs=1$ by the open-retract lemma. The derived adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,M[j])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(i^*Q,E|_U[j])$. The latter vanishes eventually, and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,E|_U[j])$ is its retract (precompose with $r$ and then $s$). Thus $E|_U$ satisfies every perfect test, so $\mathcal P(U)$ implies it is bounded below. The assumptions $\mathcal P(V)$ and $\mathcal P(U\times_WV)$ are permitted but unnecessary in this strengthened square argument.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, final paragraph, with 09IX applied to each perfect test on U rather than just a chosen generator.

proof.text: Since $E|_U$ is bounded below, choose a bounded-below K-injective representative $I$ by the ringed-site bounded injective resolution lemma. The complex $i_*I$ computes $M=Ri_*(E|_U)$ and remains bounded below, since an additive functor takes zero objects to zero objects in the same degrees. Hence $M$ is bounded below. The comparison $\tau_{\le a}E\simeq\tau_{\le a}M$ then gives $\mathcal H^j(E)=0$ for $j<\min(c,a+1)$, where $c$ is any lower bound for $M$. This verifies $\mathcal P(W)$. The induction principle now proves $\mathcal P(X)$. Apply it to the all-perfect tests for $K$ from step 3, obtaining (ii) implies (i). Together with steps 1--2, this proves all three equivalences.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, concluding paragraph: bounded-below direct image and final truncation argument.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GFI, proposition-detecting-bounded-below, with the all-perfect-test induction written explicitly; Tag 0GFG.
